newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan to cut bread prices 10 percent in January.
newsitem.headline: Jordan to cut bread prices 10 percent in January.

text.p: Jordan plans to cut the cost of bread by 10 percent at the start of next year, using low world prices to soften price hikes that sparked riots in August, the official news agency said on Monday.
Minister of Supply Munir Sobar was quoted by Petra news agency as saying Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti asked him on Monday to "work towards reducing bread prices by the start of next month."

Sobar said a ministry study showed the government could cut the price of bread, a main food for poorer Jordanians, by 20 fils (three U.S. cents) to 170 fils per kilo, and to 200 fils for bread made from higher quality flour.
Jordan, following advice from the International Monetary Fund, virtually doubled bread prices in August to slash its ballooning bill for grain import subsidies as world prices reached record highs.
Modest compensation offered to the most needy failed to prevent the worst unrest in the impoverished south of the country since riots in 1989, also sparked by price rises.
The drop in prices follows a promise to cut prices of basic imported commodities, including wheat and sugar, when world grain markets soften.

Officials said as part of its wider overhaul of subsidies -- which had included ending the state monopoly on importing grain in August -- Jordan was ending sugar sales to the private sector as traders own imports now covered local needs.

Jordan last month cut by 7.5 percent the price of fodder for livestock owners to soften a 33 percent price rise in yellow corn in August that accompanied the bread price hike. Many pastoral Jordanians are nomadic Bedouins for whom livestock rearing is the main income.
